clue.text: Loose cover across middle of deck

indicators.note: the cover stretches across, so it goes round the other letters

parts.note: to insure something is to cover it against loss

indicators.note: the central letters of the word deck, dropping its first and last

explanation.surface: A card player's protective cover has slipped off partway through the pack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' is the containment signal: the cover spreads over the centre of the deck.
explanation.definitionFit: Something insecure is not firmly fixed, which is what loose means of a fitting.

clue.text: Thoroughly maintain home with sibling I'm hesitant to leave

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: those letters leave, so they are removed from the word

parts.note: a sister is a sibling
er is the sound a hesitant speaker makes

explanation.surface: Someone insists on staying home with a sibling, reluctant to go out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' takes ER out of SISTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To insist is to assert or demand firmly and persistently.

clue.text: Dried fruit starts to top exports for Brunei, perhaps

parts.note: a sultana is a dried grape

indicators.note: the starting letters of the two words top and exports

explanation.surface: Raisins and sultanas head the export list of a small Asian state.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunei is a state ruled by a sultan, an example of a sultanate.

clue.text: Scientist injecting half of mice in upper body

indicators.note: the half is injected into the other word

parts.note: the chest is the upper body

indicators.note: the first half of the four-letter word mice

explanation.surface: A researcher injects half the lab mice in the torso.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injecting' is the containment signal, though the surface makes it sound like a lab procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemist is a scientist who studies substances and their reactions.

clue.text: Mature Brie open and denied all outsiders

indicators.note: each of the three words loses its outer letters, leaving the inside

explanation.surface: A Brie left to age, once opened, and kept away from strangers.
explanation.definitionFit: To ripen is to become fully developed, as cheese and fruit do with age.

clue.text: Officer carrying bladed tools is most careless

indicators.note: the officer carries the tools, so they sit within his letters

parts.note: LT is the abbreviation for lieutenant, a military officer
axes are tools with a blade

explanation.surface: An officer who lugs axes around is the most negligent of the bunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' is the containment signal: the officer holds the tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Lax means slack or negligent; the superlative is the one showing the least care.

clue.text: Resisting touching

definitions.meaning: ... means in contact with, as leaning ... a wall

explanation.definitionFit: The preposition covers both opposition and physical contact, as in pushing against a door.

clue.text: Run off from band with upcoming record

parts.note: ELO, Electric Light Orchestra, a rock band

indicators.note: in a down answer, coming up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Fleeing from a group that has a new release due out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upcoming' turns EP into PE.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is to run away secretly, usually to marry.

clue.text: Animation from Conservative's disheartened another

indicators.note: the heart, the middle letter, is taken out

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party, with the possessive S
another Conservative, so another Tory

explanation.surface: A cartoon about a dispirited Tory and a party colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' takes the central R out of TORYS; TORY is the everyday name for a British Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Toy Story is the 1995 Pixar film, an example of computer animation.

clue.text: Really not on being deprived

parts.note: badly means very much, as in wanting something badly
off is the opposite of on

explanation.surface: It is truly unacceptable to be left in want.
explanation.definitionFit: Being badly off means poor or lacking things, so deprived.

clue.text: Fell on taxpayers to sort out — that's obvious

indicators.note: sorting out the letters puts them into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A tax burden landing on ordinary payers needs fixing, and the case for it speaks for itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to sort out' signals rearranging all fifteen letters of FELL ON TAXPAYERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something needing no further explanation is plain on its face, so it is clear without being spelled out.

clue.text: Stop drug that tackles nothing

indicators.note: the drug tackles, taking hold of, the nothing so it sits inside

parts.note: a statin is a cholesterol-lowering drug
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A medicine that does nothing should be discontinued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that tackles' puts O inside STATIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A station is a stopping place on a railway or bus route.

clue.text: Forgiving fast about a German turning

indicators.note: the fast goes about, round, the other letters

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting

indicators.note: the German word is turned round to read the other way

parts.note: ein is German for a

explanation.surface: Someone fasting forgives a German who changed sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses the German word to NIE, and 'about' puts it within the fast; Lent is the forty days before Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: A lenient person is merciful and not harsh in judgment, ready to pardon.

clue.text: Succeeded opposing work on area for capital city

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece on another follows it

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies
anti means against, opposing
go means work or function, as a machine goes

explanation.surface: A successor who objects to labour in the region pushes for a capital.
explanation.walkthrough: SANTIAGO is the capital of Chile.
explanation.definitionFit: Santiago is the Chilean capital, a specific example of a national seat of government.

clue.text: Flier bearing bow mounted on paper

indicators.note: in a down answer, on means placed above

parts.note: air means bearing or manner

indicators.note: in a down answer, mounted means read upwards

parts.note: a bow is an arc shape
FT, the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: A flying archer carries a bow up on top of a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounted' turns ARC into CRA.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft flies, so it can be called a flier.

clue.text: Show disapproval with introduction to alternative teacher

indicators.note: the tut is introduced to, placed in front of, the alternative

parts.note: tut is the clicking sound of disapproval
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A disapproving reaction greets the arrival of a replacement teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor is a private instructor, someone who teaches a pupil or small group.

clue.text: Reference book has uterus misspelled

indicators.note: letters spelled wrongly are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry gets the spelling of uterus wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus lists words grouped by meaning, a book one consults rather than reads.

clue.text: Eccentric in close possesses ten dictionaries

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the ten inside
eccentric means odd, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: A quirky neighbour on a cul-de-sac owns ten word books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' makes LEICONS from IN CLOSE; 'possesses' puts X inside. A close is a British dead-end street.
explanation.definitionFit: A lexicon is a dictionary, especially of an ancient language.

clue.text: Head off from tunnels carrying waste containers

indicators.note: the head, the first letter, is taken off the word

parts.note: sewers are underground channels for waste

explanation.surface: Someone heads away from the sewage tunnels with some containers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off from' drops the S from SEWERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ewers are large jugs, a kind of vessel for holding water.

clue.text: Attack from south-east with no place to retreat

parts.note: SE is the compass abbreviation for south-east

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: to put is to place

explanation.surface: An assault from the south-east leaves defenders nowhere to fall back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to retreat' turns NOPUT into TUPON.
explanation.definitionFit: To set upon someone is to assault them suddenly.

clue.text: Natural responses about ego, accepting ex back

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: the reversed self takes the ex inside it
the word self is read backwards

parts.note: the ego is the self
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tale of instinctive reactions when a self-regarding person takes a former partner back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses ego's synonym into FLES, and 'accepting' takes the ex inside, giving FLEXES.
explanation.definitionFit: Reflexes are automatic, involuntary reactions of the body to a stimulus.

clue.text: Permit European quietly aboard cutter

indicators.note: the quiet letter goes on board, inside the other word

parts.note: a mower cuts grass
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A European is allowed to sail on a small vessel without fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutter' looks like a boat, but it is a lawnmower.
explanation.definitionFit: To empower someone is to give them authority to act, so to allow it.

clue.text: A pie-filling supplier's in dispute

parts.note: Sweeney Todd, the demon barber whose victims filled Mrs Lovett's pies, with the possessive S

explanation.surface: A pie maker's wholesaler is caught up in a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweeney Todd is the murderous barber of Victorian legend whose victims went into meat pies.
explanation.definitionFit: Parties at odds are disagreeing, so the phrase means in conflict.

clue.text: Some heretic niggles revolutionary agitator

indicators.note: the letters are turned round, read backwards
only some of the letters of the words heretic niggles are taken

explanation.surface: Small heretical gripes stir up a rebel rabble-rouser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks ERETICNI from heretic niggles; 'revolutionary' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: An inciter stirs people up to act, the work of a troublemaker or rabble-rouser.

clue.text: Talkative with hour spent backbiting

indicators.note: the hour is spent, used up and gone from the word

parts.note: chatty means talkative

explanation.surface: A gossip spends an hour bad-mouthing others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spent' takes H out of CHATTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Catty remarks are spiteful and malicious, the stuff of talking behind someone's back.

clue.text: A winding path's blocked by large surface material

indicators.note: the large letter blocks the path, standing in its way inside it
a winding path twists, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of path's, apostrophe dropped
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A twisting footpath obstructed by something big, and the material underfoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winding' makes SPHAT from PATHS; 'blocked by' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphalt is a tarry mix laid down for roads and paths.

clue.text: Hate Barbara regularly coming round house

indicators.note: the chosen letters come round the house, enclosing it
regular letters of the name Barbara, every other one

explanation.surface: Someone loathes it when Barbara pops round to the house so often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second, fourth and sixth letters of the name; 'coming round' wraps them about the house.
explanation.definitionFit: To abhor is to loathe or detest intensely.

clue.text: Delighted coping with society

parts.note: to be on top of a task is to be coping with it
the world means society at large, as in the ways of the world

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled at managing to get along with other people.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel on top of the world is an idiom for being elated.

clue.text: Noticing outline of prey hidden in grass

indicators.note: the outline of prey is tucked inside the other word

parts.note: to sing is slang for to inform, as does a grass

indicators.note: the outline is the outside, the first and last letters of the word prey

explanation.surface: A predator spots the shape of its quarry concealed in the long grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' looks like vegetation, but grass and sing are both slang for informing on someone; 'hidden in' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Spying something is catching sight of it, so the participle means noticing.

clue.text: Male entering nicks parts for furniture

indicators.note: the male goes into the other word

parts.note: to nick is slang for to arrest

explanation.surface: A man breaks into a shop and steals bits of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nicks' looks like stealing, but it is the slang verb for arresting someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Armrests are the parts of chairs and sofas on which one leans an arm.
